digest.component_or_area: Pass-1 plan review / LLM agent pool
propositions: Pass-1 submits all chunks and agent futures concurrently to a 6-wide pool, causing redundant cache writes of the byte-identical system prefix when cache is cold (measured ~7.9N tokens vs ideal ~2.15N, ~3.7x overage).
The warm-then-fan-out pattern is implemented for container bins but not the main Pass-1 pool; it eliminates redundant prefix writes by warming the cache serially before fanning out remaining work.

When estimated shared-prefix tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS and Pass-1 calls >= 2, the first chunk runs serially to warm the cache, then the remainder submit to the pool; below thresholds or with a single call, behavior is unchanged.
Non-systemic warm-call failures degrade gracefully to direct fan-out of remaining work; systemic LLMUnavailableError aborts the review.
Cache efficiency is verified via per-call usage records: shared prefix incurs one cache write and N-1 cache reads across N concurrent calls.
